title: Gate emission runtime
statement: Let $w$ be a finite Boolean input, let $s=(\phi,z,a,b)$ be an emitter state, let $\kappa$ be a gate kind, let $c\in\{0,1,2\}$ be a gate code, and let $i\le |w|$. For any natural number $M$ such that $z,a,b\le M$, and any output string $out$, there is a number of steps $T\le 200(M+1)$ after which the emitter machine, started in its gate-emission state with program counter zero, input-head position corresponding to $i$, unary work tapes and work-head positions encoding $(z,a,b)$, and output $out$, is in its read state with phase $g$, vertex counter $z+1$, both argument counters zero, the same input-head position, unary work tapes and work-head positions encoding $(z+1,0,0)$, and output equal to $out$ followed by the bits emitted for gate kind $\kappa$, code $c$, and counters $(z,a,b)$.
hypotheses_covered: each coordinate of $s$ is at most $M$
